assumptions.assumption: The campaign summary is the CRM-reconciled record of lifetime outcomes. The daily table is a partial, same-day view of outcomes.
assumptions.why: Spend and clicks match exactly across the two tables but daily outcomes are a small fraction of summary outcomes.
assumptions.if_wrong: If the daily table is the truth, every efficiency number in the brief is overstated and the first job is fixing the summary.

assumptions.assumption: 'Last week' is the 7 days ending on the latest date in the data, compared with the 7 days before.
assumptions.why: It is what a live weekly run would see. Full 7-day windows absorb the weekday pattern.
assumptions.if_wrong: The window is defined in one function (build_windows). Nothing else changes.

assumptions.assumption: Anything the source flags as immature is excluded from performance judgments and efficiency benchmarks.
assumptions.why: Qualified leads inside the window are about a quarter complete when measured against each campaign's own history.
assumptions.if_wrong: If the lag is longer than the flag suggests, recent campaigns will look worse than they are for longer.

assumptions.assumption: Pipeline per dollar is the primary success metric, supported by cost per opportunity and ARR per dollar. CTR, CPC and cost per lead are diagnostics only.
assumptions.why: The brief asks for qualified pipeline, opportunities and revenue over click metrics.
assumptions.if_wrong: Change outcome_metrics in config. Rankings are recomputed.

assumptions.assumption: In the experiment log the first-named arm is the variant, so 'Win' on 'A vs B' means A beat B.
assumptions.why: Every note in the log that names a winner is consistent with this reading.
assumptions.if_wrong: The direction of each learning flips. Trust tiers do not change.

assumptions.assumption: Absolute dollar magnitudes are synthetic. Ratios between segments are the signal.
assumptions.why: The data dictionary says the data is synthetic, and pipeline per dollar is implausibly high in absolute terms.

assumptions.assumption: An experiment needs at least 14 days and a sample of 100 to count as a read; a new test needs at least 28 days.
assumptions.why: Two weekly cycles is the floor for any read, and pipeline outcomes need longer than lead outcomes.
assumptions.if_wrong: These are defaults in config for the marketing lead to set.

assumptions.assumption: No proposed test may exceed the highest daily budget the team has already run, or a fixed total budget ceiling.
assumptions.why: The agent should never ask for more exposure than the team has already chosen to take.
assumptions.if_wrong: Raise the ceilings in config. Approval is still required for every launch.

reliability_levels.final: Settled data. Safe to act on.
reliability_levels.provisional: Inside the attribution lag window. Will still change.
reliability_levels.observational: A pattern across campaigns, not a controlled test. Shows where to test, not what is true.
reliability_levels.modeled: An estimate from a stated formula. Not an observed result.
reliability_levels.data_quality: A known problem with the data and how the agent handles it.

signals.title: Google budget moved from Webinar to Demo
signals.statement: In the last 8 weeks Google Webinar fell from 55% to 5% of platform spend while Demo rose from 42% to 92%. In settled campaigns Google Webinar returns 3.2x the pipeline per dollar of Google Demo. The only test favoring Demo (E013) is rejected as a false winner.
signals.test_angle: Head-to-head Webinar vs Demo on Google, same audience and theme, read on pipeline per dollar after attribution settles.
cautions: The mix shift is a fact. Why it happened is not in the data.

signals.title: E013 is logged as a win but is not a valid read
signals.statement: E013 (Demo vs webinar, Google) is logged as Win +15% but is not a valid read: ran 5 days (minimum 14); sample of 31 (minimum 100); primary metric 'Lead conversion rate' is a proxy, not a business outcome; logged confidence is Low. Campaign data disagrees: Demo returns 0.31x the pipeline per dollar of Webinar in settled campaigns on Google (18 vs 15 campaigns).
signals.test_angle: Re-run 'Demo vs webinar' at full length and sample on an outcome metric before acting on it.
cautions: Until re-run, this result should be removed from the team's list of learnings.

signals.title: Google beats comparable campaigns
signals.statement: Google (platform) returns 1.86x the pipeline of comparable campaigns, above benchmark in all 3 cells with enough spend. It takes 31% of settled spend and 37% of the last 8 weeks' spend. Like for like, that is pipeline worth 29% of the program total gained (modeled).
signals.test_angle: Controlled test that scales Google against the current mix, measured on pipeline per dollar.
cautions: Observational gap. Confirms where to test, not the size of the win.

signals.test_angle: Controlled test that moves budget away from Demo toward the stronger alternative, measured on pipeline per dollar.
cautions: Observational gap. Confirms where to test, not the size of the win.

cautions: Fatigue is measured on CTR. Whether it carries through to pipeline is untested.

evidence.title: Daily and summary files disagree on outcomes
evidence.statement: Spend, impressions and clicks reconcile exactly between the daily and summary tables, but the daily table carries only 16% of conversions, 13% of qualified leads, 4% of opportunities and 3.5% of pipeline.
caveats: Handling: lifetime efficiency (pipeline per dollar, cost per opportunity) comes from the campaign summary only.
Handling: the daily table is used for delivery trends and for comparing a campaign with itself over time.
Handling: outcome levels from the two tables are never combined in one calculation.
Assumption A1: the summary is the CRM-reconciled record; daily outcomes are a partial same-day view.

evidence.title: Some campaigns have no daily outcome data at all
evidence.statement: 20 campaigns show zero conversions in the daily table while the summary credits them with 2,403 (20 on LinkedIn), and 73 campaigns with opportunities in the summary show none in the daily table.
caveats: Handling: a zero in the daily outcome columns is treated as 'not reported', never as 'no result'.

evidence.title: Daily rows with missing CRM pipeline and ARR
evidence.statement: 45 of 5,691 daily rows (0.8%) across 38 campaigns have no pipeline or ARR value, covering $26,453 of spend and 6 opportunities.
caveats: Handling: missing values stay missing. They are excluded from pipeline rates and never filled with zero.

evidence.title: Inconsistent audience labels
evidence.statement: 12 of 128 campaigns use a non-standard audience label (Enterprise Legal, IH MM, LF ENT, Law Firm MM). The agent's alias map resolves 128 of 128 campaigns to the same label as the source's cleaned field.
caveats: Handling: all analysis groups on the canonical label. An unknown label is surfaced, not guessed.

evidence.title: Recent downstream data is incomplete
evidence.statement: Everything from Jun 17 to Jun 30 is inside the attribution lag window (source flag). Measured against each campaign's own prior 28 days, conversions in the window are 96% of what their clicks would normally produce, but qualified leads are only 27% of what their conversions would normally produce (10 of 10 comparable campaigns are below their own baseline). Lead capture is current; qualification and everything after it is not. 14 campaigns carry the immature flag in the summary.
caveats: Handling: for the reporting week only spend, impressions, clicks and conversions are treated as final.
Handling: qualified leads, opportunities and pipeline for the window are shown as provisional and never used to judge performance.
Handling: campaigns flagged immature are excluded from efficiency benchmarks.

evidence.title: Campaign-to-experiment links are unreliable
evidence.statement: Of 60 campaigns linked to an experiment, 42 point to an experiment that ran on a different platform and 30 did not overlap the experiment's dates.
caveats: Handling: linked_experiment_id is not used to attribute campaign results to an experiment.

evidence.title: creative_age_days measures campaign age, not creative exposure
evidence.statement: creative_age_days equals days since campaign launch in 100% of rows and tops out at 70 days, yet 30 creatives ran in more than one campaign and the most reused have been in market for up to 172 days.
caveats: Handling: fatigue is measured within a campaign. True audience exposure to a reused creative is longer than the field suggests.

evidence.title: Campaign format does not always match the creative library
evidence.statement: 45 campaigns report a format that differs from their creative's library format. 43 are Google campaigns, where the field holds the ad type (RSA, Responsive Display) rather than the creative format. 2 are genuine mismatches on other platforms (C081, C095).
caveats: Handling: format comparisons exclude Google.

evidence.title: Flags carried in the source data
evidence.statement: Campaign-level flags in the summary: High volume / low quality (42), Attribution immature (14), Under-tested theme (8).

evidence.title: Reporting week versus prior week
evidence.statement: In the week of Jun 24 to Jun 30, 9 campaigns spent $17,013 (-53% vs the prior week's $36,140 across 14 campaigns), producing 11,713 clicks (-64%) and 86 conversions (-67%).
caveats: Qualified leads, opportunities and pipeline for both weeks are provisional (see DQ.attribution_lag).
Daily conversion counts are a partial view (see DQ.reconciliation). Week-over-week direction is valid; absolute levels are not comparable with the campaign summary.

evidence.title: Why spend changed
evidence.statement: Spend moved -$19,126 week over week. 8 campaigns that ended or wound down account for -$19,000 of it (99%); the 6 campaigns live all 14 days moved -$126; 0 campaigns launched.

evidence.title: Like-for-like performance
evidence.statement: For the 6 campaigns live through both weeks, spend was -1%, CTR moved from 2.18% to 1.97% (-10%) and conversions went from 60 to 57.
